turns.assessment: The failure is localized to the launch of OMS S06->S19. Input and output power disappeared at every amplifier, including the booster input, while all amplifier pump currents remained unchanged; therefore the loss originates before amp0 rather than in an amplifier or downstream span. Simultaneous loss of all channels and the resulting downstream OCH LOS/service failures are best explained by a disconnected/broken OMS input patch at S06.

proposals.rationale: The input to the first amplifier on S06->S19 is lost, all downstream amplifier powers and channels are lost, and pump currents are unchanged. This is the exact signature of the OMS input patch at S06 being disconnected or broken.
A ROADM port failure could block multiple channels before the booster, but the complete loss at the OMS launch is more directly explained by its input patch.
A failed booster could remove downstream output, but it would not explain loss of measured input power at amp0, and its pump-current telemetry did not change.
A cut in the first span would darken downstream receivers, but amp0 input and normally its output should remain present, contrary to the observations.
